newsitem.title: USA: Lexmark set to exceed full year estimates.
newsitem.headline: Lexmark set to exceed full year estimates.

text.p: Lexmark International Group Inc said on Monday it expected full year earnings to exceed analyst consensus estimates and that capital spending would be at least 25 percent under full year estimates.

"Spending will underrun our initial estimates as a result of aggressive management of capital projects, some rebalancing of production plans and changes in timing of implementation," said Marvin Mann, chairman and chief executive officer.

The company, which reported third quarter 1996 earnings of $0.40 per share against $0.21 per share in the same quarter last year, said its strong performance was due to a successful printing solutions strategy and a focus on manufacturing and operating costs.
Operating income was boosted by strength in the core printer and consumables business, Mann said.
The First Call mean earnings estimate for the fourth quarter was $0.52 per share and $1.51 for the fiscal year.
"We are pleased with our performance this quarter, the company's financial position remains strong, and we are well-positioned for future growth," Mann said.

"Last year, we had a more favorable IBM supplies distribution agreement, very strong printer shipments, and operating income from the keyboard business contributing to fourth quarter results," he said. "Despite the income contributions from those product areas in 1995, we believe we will achieve or possibly exceed those record earnings in the fourth quarter this year."
In the first nine months of 1996, revenues from printers and associated supplies increased 25 percent against the same period last year, the company said.

Mann said the retail environment for inkjet printers remained very competitive but pricing pressures moderated during the third quarter and shipments of Lexmark's inkjet printers strengthened in the last two months of the quarter.
